acv.quote: We proposed six hundred K a year.

header.reason: Adyen won because COO Angela, who signed and whom we met only once, wanted proof that stores would work: a live till return, a rollout plan and retail references. Adyen brought a team that had done store rollouts; we described the return and said a partner would do installs. Tom believes we 'won the web side', but this was one contract and all of it went to Adyen.

findings.label: What started it
findings.finding: Aim messaging at the post-holiday moment when stores can't process buy-online-return-in-store and the loyalty program breaks across store and web.
findings.quote: The store couldn't see the online order, so staff were refunding to gift cards or telling people to mail it back.

findings.label: Who decided
findings.finding: Get reps to the COO and store operations early, and show them store returns and rollout working, not only the CTO's web requirements.

findings.label: The competitor
findings.finding: Pre-empt a retail rollout team by bringing named people who have run store rollouts to store workshops; this rests on Raj's account to Tom.
findings.quote: He said they came in with a retail team, people who'd done store rollouts, and they talked about one platform for the tills and the website, on one contract.

findings.label: Our message
findings.finding: Replace the 'line between them has pretty much disappeared' slide with a step-by-step till return walkthrough, and keep the online checkout demo.

findings.label: Missing proof
findings.finding: Build a live online-order return at a store till, a store rollout plan with dates and installers, and retail references ready to call.

findings.label: Their words
findings.finding: Use 'the tills' and 'one system for the tills and the website' instead of 'unified commerce', 'point of sale' and 'in-person payments'.
findings.quote: One system for the tills and the website.
